Declare the text field with `Form` and the file with `File` (or `UploadFile`) in the same *path operation*. Use `File` and `Form` together when you need to receive data and files in the same request.[1]

First, to receive uploaded files and/or form data, first install [`python-multipart`](https://github.com/Kludex/python-multipart).[2]

```console
$ uv add python-multipart
```

Here's the docs' example adapted to a title and an attachment:

```python
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import FastAPI, File, Form, UploadFile

app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/files/")
async def create_file(
    title: Annotated[str, Form()],
    attachment: Annotated[UploadFile, File()],
):
    return {
        "title": title,
        "attachment_content_type": attachment.content_type,
    }
```

The files and form fields will be uploaded as form data and you will receive the files and form fields.[2] And you can declare some of the files as `bytes` and some as `UploadFile`.[2]

If you'd rather group the text fields in a Pydantic model, you can also combine a form model with file parameters[4], for example `profile: Annotated[Profile, Form()], avatar: UploadFile`.

**Note:** You can declare multiple `File` and `Form` parameters in a *path operation*, but you can't also declare `Body` fields that you expect to receive as JSON, as the request will have the body encoded using `multipart/form-data` instead of `application/json`.[2]
